compiled by imperial decree.
Afterwards, Xuétiāntái.
Tàizōng Míng Huángdì, Superior, Part One.
His given name was Yù,
courtesy name Xiūjǐng,
and pet name Róngqī.
He was the eleventh son of Wén Dì.
First Year of Tàishǐ (Yǐsì, 465).
1. Spring,
First month,
On the first day of Yǐwèi,
the deposed emperor changed the era name to Yǒngguāng,
and issued a general amnesty.
In the eighth month of this year,
Jiāngxià Wáng Yìgōng, Liǔ Yuánjǐng, and Yán Shībó were killed.
The era name was changed to Jǐnghé.
After assassinating the deposed emperor,
the era name was changed to Tàishǐ.
In one year, the era name was changed three times.
2. On Bǐngshēn,
Wèi issued a great amnesty.
3. Second month,
On Dīngchǒu,
the Wèi ruler went to Lóufán Gōng.
Lóufán Xiàn
belonged to Yànmén Jùn during the Hàn dynasty.
Wèi and Jìn abandoned it to the desolate wilderness.
Wèi Shōu's Dìxíng Zhì states: Yànmén Jùn's Yuánpíng Xiàn had Lóufán Chéng.
Xián says: The old city of Lóufán
is northeast of modern Dàizhōu Guōxiàn.
I observe from Táng Shū:
Xiàn Zhōu
was the ancient land of Lóufán.
4. Since Xiàojiàn,
people had been secretly minting counterfeit and debased coins.
This began in the second year of Xiàowǔ Dì's Xiàojiàn era, recorded in Volume 128.
On Gēngyín,
two-zhū coins were re-minted,
and their form became increasingly thin.
Whenever official coins were issued,
people immediately imitated them,
making them even thinner and smaller,
without rims or borders,
and not filed or polished.
They were called
"Lěizǐ."
Lǜ,
pronounced like "liáo jù,"
means a file.
Lěi,
pronounced like "lú duì."
Dù Yòu's Tōngdiǎn
writes "Lěizǐ"
as
"Láizǐ."
5. Third month,
On Yǐsì,
the Wèi ruler returned to Píngchéng.
6. Summer,
Fifth month,
On Guǐmǎo,
Wèi Gāozōng died.
He was twenty-six years old
and was posthumously given the title Wénchéng Huángdì.
Wèi Shìzǔ had campaigned in all directions,
and the state was quite depleted.
Moreover, with internal strife,
both court and populace were in distress.
Chǔchǔ
describes a sorrowful and pained appearance.
Cháo,
pronounced like "zhí yáo."
He adapted to the times,
where xiāo means decline;
and xī means growth.
He united the country,
and the people's hearts returned to peace.
On Jiǎchén,
Crown Prince Hóng ascended the imperial throne.
Hóng
was Wénchéng Dì's eldest son.
Xiāo Zǐxiǎn states: Hóng's
courtesy name was Wànmín.
The empress was honored as empress dowager.
Xiǎnzǔ
Wèi Xiànwén Dì's temple name was Xiǎnzǔ.
Shìzhōng, Chējì Dàjiàngjūn Yǐ Hún monopolized power,
forging an imperial edict to kill Shàngshū Yáng Bǎonián, Píngyáng Gōng Jiǎ Àirén, and Nányáng Gōng Zhāng Tiāndù within the palace.
Shìzhōng, Sītú, Píngyuán Wáng Lù Lì was recuperating from an illness at the Hot Springs of Dàijùn.
The Wèi Tǔdì Jì states: ninety lǐ north of Dài City is Sānggān City.
West of the city, crossing the Sānggān River,
ten lǐ from Sānggān City,
there are hot springs,
effective for healing illnesses.
Zhì (治),
read as zhí (直).
The Wèi official system included the Sīwèi Jiān,
in charge of guarding the palace.
"Hún has a heart that disregards his lord.
Now that the emperor has passed away,
your Highness's prestige and virtue have always been highly regarded.
For the establishment of Wèi Gāozōng,
Lì rendered meritorious service,
and moreover, he is loyal and sincere,
hence his prestige and virtue are greatly esteemed at this time.
It would be advisable to delay your return for a short while to observe the situation;
when the court is tranquil,
then enter,
it will not be too late."
Lì said:
"How can one hear of the death of one's sovereign and father, and, out of concern for trouble, not rush to attend?"
He immediately galloped to Píngchéng.
Yǐ Hún's actions were mostly unlawful,
and Lì repeatedly contended with him.
On the day Wùshēn,
Hún again killed Lì and Mù Duōhóu.
Duōhóu
was Shòu's younger brother.
Mù Shòu served Wèi Shìzǔ
and was enfeoffed as Yídū Wáng.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Wèi appointed Hún as Tàiwèi and Lù Shàngshū Shì,
Liú Ní, the Dōng'ān Wáng, as Sītú,
and Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè Dàirén Hé Qínú as Sīkōng.
Diànzhōng Shàngshū, Shùnyáng Gōng Yù, plotted to execute Yǐ Hún,
but Hún killed him.
The lord was young and the state was uncertain,
treacherous officials seized power,
slaughtering loyal and virtuous men;
it was fortunate that Wèi did not perish.
7. On the day Rénzǐ,
Wèi appointed Huáinán Wáng Tā as Zhènxī Dàjiàngjūn and Yítóng Sānsī,
to guard Liángzhōu.
8. Wèi
lifted the alcohol prohibition.
Wèi had imposed an alcohol prohibition,
as seen in Volume 128, Xiàowǔ Xiàojiàn 3rd year.
9. On the day Rénwǔ,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng was given the additional title of Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ,
and Yán Shībó was given the additional title of Dānyáng Yǐn.
10. In autumn,
seventh month,
on the day Guǐsì,
Wèi appointed Tàiwèi Yǐ Hún as Chéngxiàng,
ranking him above all princes;
all matters, great or small,
were decided by Hún.
11. The Deposed Emperor was young and impetuous.
Upon ascending the throne,
he initially still feared the empress dowager, senior ministers, and Dài Fǎxīng and others,
not daring to act arbitrarily.
After the empress dowager's death,
last year,
the empress dowager died.
When he wished to do something,
Fǎxīng would always restrain him,
saying to the emperor:
"Your Majesty's actions are like this,
do you wish to become Yíngyáng?"
The matter of Yíngyáng Wáng is seen in Volume 120, Wéndì Yuánjiā 1st year.
The Deposed Emperor was inherently wild and violent,
and Dài Fǎxīng's words were enough to bring about his death.
He favored the eunuch Huà Yuàn'ér,
bestowing countless gifts,
but Fǎxīng always reduced them,
which Yuàn'ér resented.
The emperor sent Yuàn'ér outside to observe public opinion,
and Yuàn'ér reported to the emperor:
"The roads all say: 'There are two Sons of Heaven in the palace: Fǎxīng is the true
Son of Heaven,
and Your Majesty is a counterfeit Son of Heaven.'
Moreover, Your Majesty resides in the deep palace,
not interacting with people.
Fǎxīng, along with Tàizǎi, Yán, and Liǔ, act as one body,
Yìgōng holds the position of Lù Shàngshū Shì,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng is Shàngshū Lìng,
Yán Shībó is Púyè,
and all matters are exclusively decided by Fǎxīng,
hence the saying.
Officials and commoners, both inside and outside the court, all fear and obey him.
Fǎxīng was a close associate of Xiàowǔ,
having been in the inner palace for a long time;
now he has formed a clique with others,
and I deeply fear that this seat of power may no longer belong to Your Majesty."
The emperor then issued an edict to dismiss Fǎxīng.
Dismissed means
dismissed from his current office.
He was then exiled to a distant commandery.
In the eighth month,
on the day Xīnyǒu,
Fǎxīng was granted death;
Cháo Shàngzhī was relieved of his position as Shèrén.
Cháo Shàngzhī had been Zhōngshū Tōngshì Shèrén since Xiàowǔ's time.
Yuánwài Sànqí Shìláng, Dōnghǎi Xī Xiǎndù,
was also favored by Shìzǔ.
He often supervised construction projects,
and his supervision was harsh and cruel,
with beatings and torture,
which everyone suffered from.
The emperor often jokingly said:
"Xiǎndù is a bane to the people,
he should be eliminated soon."
His attendants then assented,
and an imperial decree was immediately announced to kill him.
Shàngshū Yòu Púyè, Lǐng Wèiwèi Qīng, Dānyáng Yǐn Yán Shībó had held power for a long time.
In the 4th year of Dàmíng of Xiàowǔ,
Yán Shībó was summoned from Lìchéng,
promoted from Shìzhōng to Shàngshū Púyè,
holding a vital position.
He was extravagant and self-indulgent,
disliked by the gentry.
The emperor wanted to personally attend to government affairs,
on the day Gēngwǔ,
he appointed Shībó as Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè,
relieving him of Qīng and Yǐn,
relieving him of Wèiwèi Qīng and Dānyáng Yǐn.
Dividing his authority.
Shībó then became afraid.
Originally,
Shìzǔ was very suspicious,
and princes, dukes, and senior ministers, trembled and held their breath,
none daring to visit each other presumptuously.
When Shìzǔ died,
Tàizǎi Yìgōng and others all congratulated each other, saying:
"Today we are finally free from violent death."
Immediately after the funeral,
Yìgōng, along with Liǔ Yuánjǐng and Yán Shībó, indulged in music, singing, and heavy drinking,
day and night without stopping;
the emperor was internally displeased.
After killing Dài Fǎxīng,
all the senior ministers were shaken with fear,
each feeling insecure;
thereupon, Yuánjǐng and Shībó secretly plotted to depose the emperor
and establish Yìgōng.
They gathered day and night to plot,
but hesitated and could not make a decision.
Yuánjǐng disclosed his plot to Shěn Qìngzhī;
Qìngzhī and Yìgōng had never been close,
and Shībó often monopolized court affairs,
not consulting Qìngzhī,
saying to his clerks:
(Shàngshū Lìngshǐ, literally, secretary of the Imperial Secretariat.)
"Shěn Gōng is merely a talon and tooth,
how can he participate in political matters!"
Qìngzhī resented this,
